we cloned and characterized a novel preprohormon of C-RFa from carp, and demonstrated the prolactin-releasing activity of synthetic C-RFa in primary cultured fish pititaries, the seasonal variation of C-RFa mRNA expression in hypothalamus and the pituitary, and the distribution of C-RFa immunopositive fibers and cells in the central nervous system of carp.
we have cloned and characterized a novel prepro C-RFA cDNA from Cyprimus carpio and demonstrated that the synthetic C-RFA peptide stimulates prolactin release.
C-RFa, a neuropeptide that stimulates PRL release from fish pituitary, was cloned from carp, and its expression in brain and pituitary was modulated by seasonal acclimatization.

a new approach for studying the role of C-RFa as a prolactin-releasing hormone in the teleost pituitary.
the characterization of C-RFa as a new prolactin releasing hormone in teleosts, which may play a significant role in the seasonal modulation of PRL expression.
the identification of a novel hypothalamic peptide that could be involved in prolactin secretion in teleosts, and its potential implication in seasonal changes in prolactin release.

the C-RFa is a novel hypothalamic factor with a role in the regulation of PRL expression in teleosts.

the prolactin releasing factor C-RFa is conserved among vertebrates and is a potential candidate in the control of seasonal prolactin expression in carp.
